exam.name: AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Associate
exam.note: 50 of the 65 questions are scored; 15 are unscored pretest items you cannot identify. Scoring is scaled 100–1000, pass at 720. Domain weights are identical in C03 and C04.

modules.name: Ground rules
modules.blurb: The mental model everything else hangs off.

modules.name: Compute
modules.blurb: Where your code actually runs, and how it scales.

modules.name: Storage
modules.blurb: Object, block, file — and picking correctly under pressure.

modules.name: Networking
modules.blurb: The domain that decides most exam questions.

modules.name: Integration & ops
modules.blurb: Decoupling, observability, and the security toolbox.

modules.name: Architecting
modules.blurb: Putting it together the way the exam grades it.

lectures.title: The shape of AWS
lectures.standfirst: Regions, Availability Zones, edge locations, and who is responsible for what. Every later answer is a consequence of this geometry.

lectures.title: IAM: who may do what
lectures.standfirst: Users, roles, policies, and the evaluation logic that decides every API call in AWS. The single most-tested topic on the exam.

lectures.title: EC2 and what it costs
lectures.standfirst: Instance families, the five purchasing models, placement groups, and instance metadata. Most cost questions on the exam live here.

lectures.title: Load balancing and auto scaling
lectures.standfirst: ALB vs NLB vs GWLB, target groups, health checks, and the scaling policies that make an architecture 'resilient' in exam language.

lectures.title: Serverless and containers
lectures.standfirst: Lambda's real limits, ECS vs EKS vs Fargate, API Gateway, and the question the exam is really asking when it says 'no servers to manage'.

lectures.title: S3, properly
lectures.standfirst: Storage classes, lifecycle, versioning, encryption, access control, and performance. Expect S3 in a fifth of your questions.

lectures.title: Block and file storage
lectures.standfirst: EBS volume types and their IOPS ceilings, instance store, EFS, the FSx family, and how data gets in from on-premises.

lectures.title: VPC from first principles
lectures.standfirst: Subnets, route tables, internet and NAT gateways, security groups versus NACLs. Build the mental picture once and networking questions become mechanical.

lectures.title: Connecting VPCs and data centres
lectures.standfirst: Peering, Transit Gateway, Site-to-Site VPN, Direct Connect, VPC endpoints and PrivateLink — and the exact cue that selects each one.

lectures.title: The edge: DNS, CDN, anycast
lectures.standfirst: Route 53 routing policies, CloudFront behaviours and origin protection, and when Global Accelerator beats a CDN.

lectures.title: Relational: RDS and Aurora
lectures.standfirst: Multi-AZ versus read replicas — the distinction the exam tests over and over — plus Aurora's architecture, backups, and failover behaviour.

lectures.title: DynamoDB
lectures.standfirst: Partition keys, capacity modes, GSIs versus LSIs, DAX, Streams and Global Tables. Single-digit millisecond latency at any scale — with rules.

lectures.title: Caching and analytics
lectures.standfirst: ElastiCache Redis vs Memcached, Redshift, Athena, Glue, Kinesis, EMR, OpenSearch. Mostly a service-recognition exercise — learn the cues.

lectures.title: Decoupling: queues, topics, events
lectures.standfirst: SQS, SNS, EventBridge, Step Functions and Amazon MQ. 'Decouple' is exam code for a specific short list of answers.

lectures.title: Observability and governance
lectures.standfirst: CloudWatch vs CloudTrail vs Config — three services people confuse — plus X-Ray, Systems Manager, Organizations and Control Tower.

lectures.title: The security toolbox
lectures.standfirst: KMS and envelope encryption, Secrets Manager vs Parameter Store, ACM, WAF, Shield, GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie, and Cognito.

lectures.title: Resilience and disaster recovery
lectures.standfirst: RTO and RPO, the four DR strategies and their cost order, and how to read a resilience question in ten seconds.

lectures.title: Designing for cost
lectures.standfirst: Where the money actually goes, the levers per service, and the cost-management tools the exam names by title.

lectures.title: Migration and hybrid
lectures.standfirst: Getting servers, databases and petabytes onto AWS, and what to do when the workload cannot come at all.

lectures.title: Services you only need to recognise
lectures.standfirst: The recognition half of the paper: a job described in plain English, and the one AWS service built for it. Free marks if the map is memorised.

lectures.title: The exam playbook
lectures.standfirst: How the questions are built, the keyword-to-service map, elimination tactics, timing, and what to do in the last ten minutes.
